summary: On node1, created user datauser and a filesystem-enforced 100MB quota under /srv/data using a loopback-mounted ext4 filesystem with the native ext4 quota feature. datauser can write up to 100MB (102400 KB) under /srv/data; further writes fail with "Disk quota exceeded" at the OS/filesystem level. Verified the setup persists across a full node reboot (boot ID changed, mount and quota limit recovered automatically via fstab).
actions_performed: Created local user datauser (uid 1000) on node1
Created a 512MB ext4-backed image file /var/lib/srv-data-img/data.img and mounted it at /srv/data (loop device) with the usrquota option, registered in /etc/fstab for persistence
Enabled the native ext4 on-disk quota feature via tune2fs -O quota (avoids deprecated external quota files)
Set a 100MB (102400 KB) soft and hard block quota for datauser via setquota, and chowned /srv/data to datauser
Verified enforcement: datauser could write 90MB but a subsequent 50MB write failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' precisely at the 100MB cap; cleaned up test files
Captured pre-restart baseline (boot_id, fstab entry, active mount, repquota showing the 100MB limit)
Issued sudo systemctl reboot on node1, polled until exec access returned, and confirmed boot_id changed (67f3a44b... -> 3be1e874...) proving an actual restart occurred

Post-reboot, verified /srv/data auto-remounted with quota active and datauser's 100MB limit was still enforced (re-tested with a 110MB write, which correctly failed at the quota boundary), then cleaned up the test file

evidence.requirement: datauser account limited to 100MB under /srv/data, enforced by the filesystem
evidence.summary: Created datauser, built loopback ext4 filesystem at /srv/data with native quota feature, set 100MB user quota via setquota, and proved enforcement: a write past 100MB failed with 'Disk quota exceeded' at exactly the configured limit.
Captured boot_id, active /srv/data mount with quota option, fstab entry, and repquota output showing datauser's 100MB limit before restart.

evidence.requirement: Single-node restart acknowledgement and changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Issued systemctl reboot (ack returned then connection dropped), polled until node1 accepted exec again, and confirmed boot_id changed from 67f3a44b-85c6-40fe-8529-fcb6e8ac337a to 3be1e874-241b-4707-bcc2-a3fb499152cb, proving an actual reboot occurred.

After reboot, /srv/data auto-remounted via fstab with quota active and datauser's 100MB limit intact; a 110MB write attempt correctly failed with 'Disk quota exceeded', confirming the quota enforcement survived the restart.
